open_questions: Salesforce's public documentation does not establish whether Salesforce is currently present in the Speakeasy MCP Catalog.
The activation documentation does not publish exact SObject row labels or enabled-toggle states.
Speakeasy compatibility is standards-inferred from OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code with PKCE and needs an end-to-end connection test.

blockers.where: #enable-sobject-server — “Choose the least-privileged server that meets the team's needs:”
blockers.problem: The reader must choose a server but is not told where to obtain the team's approved read, write, or delete requirements.
blockers.suggestion: Add one sentence directing the reader to obtain the approved server choice from the application or cloud security owner when the ticket does not specify it.

blockers.problem: The guide ends with a shortened pointer instead of the canonical closing sentence recorded in the Dossier and `docs/speakeasy-setup.md`.
blockers.suggestion: Replace the final line with: This guide covers setup only. For anything beyond it — billing, tool behavior, limits — see [Salesforce's MCP documentation](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/hosted-mcp-servers/guide/hosted-mcp-servers-overview.html).

blockers.problem: The guide does not identify the exact PKCE control or the controls used to add the two required OAuth scopes.
blockers.suggestion: Research the verbatim PKCE label and scope-selection controls, then add exact click-by-click actions to the Dossier and Setup Guide.

blockers.problem: The guide supports scratch-org URLs but provides no executable browser workflow for creating, packaging, and installing the required External Client App.
blockers.suggestion: Either research and document the complete scratch-org workflow or narrow the Guide's supported setup path to org types where the app can be created directly.

nits.problem: The screenshot note omits the canonical requirement that the Add Source menu be open on the Sources page.
nits.suggestion: Restore “the Add Source menu open on the Sources page” from docs/speakeasy-setup.md.

nits.where: #connect-speakeasy-credentials — “Each call runs as the signed-in Salesforce user and follows that user's field-level security, object permissions, and sharing rules.”
nits.problem: This explanatory sentence uses Salesforce security terminology without giving the reader an action.
nits.suggestion: Replace it with an imperative such as “Sign in as a Salesforce user who has access to every record the connection needs.”

nits.problem: The PKCE control is written as plain prose while adjacent OAuth security controls use bold verbatim labels.
nits.suggestion: Render step 6 as a single action on the console label, e.g. Select **Require PKCE** (or the exact checkbox label from the Dossier if it differs).

nits.problem: The cross-link uses bold markup inside the link text (`[Salesforce **Consumer Key**](#copy-consumer-key)`), which is inconsistent with other anchor links in the guide.
nits.suggestion: Use plain link text such as Paste the [**Consumer Key**](#copy-consumer-key) into **Client ID**, matching the pattern in guides like X.

nits.problem: The guide tells the reader to complete Salesforce sign-in when prompted without identifying what action opens that prompt.
nits.suggestion: Clarify the authorization sequence using only controls established by the canonical Speakeasy setup, or record this missing Speakeasy-side transition as a doctrine open question.

nits.problem: The paragraph after step 11 states that each call runs as the signed-in user under FLS, object permissions, and sharing rules, which describes runtime behavior rather than an action required to finish setup.
nits.suggestion: Remove that paragraph from the Setup Guide; keep the authorization model in the Research Dossier only unless a setup step depends on it.

nits.problem: Two capability bullets attribute risk or safety to Salesforce ("Salesforce describes this as…" / "Salesforce describes deletion as…") instead of giving the admin a direct choice criterion.
nits.suggestion: Shorten each bullet to the capability boundary only (read/query vs create/update vs delete vs all) and drop the documentation-attribution phrases.

nits.problem: The scratch-org External Client App limitation appears in Prerequisites while the Dossier places it under {#open-salesforce-setup}, so an edge-case procedure sits before the console walkthrough most readers follow.
nits.suggestion: Delete the scratch-org sentence from Prerequisites and add a single "If you use a scratch org:" branch under {#open-salesforce-setup} with the hub, package, and install steps.

nits.problem: The phrase "the org that will expose its records" appears twice in back-to-back Prerequisites content.
nits.suggestion: Keep the phrase in one place (for example the sign-in sentence) and refer to "that org" in the System Administrator bullet.

blockers.suggestion: Select **Issue JSON Web Token (JWT)-based access tokens for named users** before **Require Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) extension for Supported Authorization Flows**.
